source_quality_note: Financial and operating facts are anchored to the formal 2026H1 report; scenario EPS, valuation multiples, probabilities and hurdle price are analytical assumptions.

financial_quality.judgment: The earnings recovery is broad and cash-backed rather than purely accounting-driven, supporting a fresh ADD case at a sufficient price discount.

balance_sheet_and_capex.judgment: Capex and leverage remain the principal counterweight: finance expense and short-term borrowings are high, so H1 margin recovery must convert into sustained free cash flow and eventual deleveraging.

business_quality.judgment: Polyurethane remains the profit anchor; petrochemical economics improved from cost/feedstock optimization, while fine chemicals/new materials add structural growth. The investment case still requires caution because some H1 supply tightness may normalize.

shareholder_return.judgment: The interim payout is supportive but secondary to the sustainability of operating cash returns after capex.

market_implied_expectation.interpretation: The price is below the fresh 15% hurdle derived from probability-weighted value, creating room for an ADD in the existing protected simulation position, subject to portfolio sizing.

thesis.core: Wanhua's H1 recovery is broad and cash-backed, with polyurethane resilience and improved petrochemical economics. At 70.78 the equity clears the 15% hurdle, but elevated debt, finance cost and capex mean the ADD thesis depends on recovery converting into durable free cash flow rather than a temporary supply-cycle windfall.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: Use FY normalized EPS bear/base/bull of RMB4.8/RMB6.4/RMB8.0, with the base case below a simple H1 annualization to reflect cyclicality and potential normalization of temporary supply tightness.
thesis.variant_wedge: The market appears to discount the durability of H1 recovery and integrated cost advantages; the counter-case is that geopolitical/supply constraints and petrochemical margin repair prove temporary while financing costs remain elevated.

catalysts: Polyurethane global share and margins remain resilient as industry supply stays rational.
Ethane-feed and integrated petrochemical optimization sustain the H1 cost advantage.
High-end fine chemicals and new materials scale with acceptable incremental ROIC.
Capex transitions toward cash returns and deleveraging while the interim payout remains sustainable.
kill_thesis: H1 profit uplift proves mainly temporary global supply disruption and core chemical spreads normalize sharply.
Debt and finance costs keep rising while free cash flow materially lags reported earnings.
Large new capex projects deliver sub-hurdle utilization or ROIC.
Core polyurethane profitability erodes structurally rather than cyclically.
